rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quote for 'AI doomers vs. builders' piece". It read: "Hi Tessa, I appreciate you reaching out. Here's a quote you're welcome to use: \"I started Halcyon Threshold because I believe superintelligence is coming and its outcome will be the most important thing that happens in this century. The labs are doing important work on capabilities, but I think they're underinvesting in the governance and coordination problems that matter most. We need diverse voices beyond the major labs thinking clearly about how to ensure this goes well — not because we're opposed to progress, but because we want to make sure progress leads somewhere good.\" You can attribute it to Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to reporter Tessa Brandt with quote for Larkin Dispatch piece

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you so much for the offer — having data and analytics support is exactly what we need right now. Here are a few concrete projects I'm thinking about that could use your skills: 1. **Landscape mapping**: Compile and organize data on AI governance, safety, and policy organizations. What's out there, who's funding them, what they focus on? This would help us identify gaps and coordination opportunities. 2. **Policy tracking**: Build a database or dashboard tracking major AI policy developments, regulations, and governance initiatives globally. What's happening where, and what's it aimed at? 3. **Grant landscape**: Research funding available for AI safety/governance work — grants, fellowships, accelerators, rapid response funds. What's available and what are the deadlines? 4. **Stakeholder analysis**: Help us understand the key players and their positions on different aspects of superintelligence development. Which of these sounds most interesting to you, or do you have other ideas? Five hours a week would be genuinely valuable for any of these. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Engaged with Priya Raman (5 hrs/week volunteer data analyst) with concrete project options

Fields: "{\"title\":\"Bridging Technical Safety and Governance: A Framework for Integration\",\"author_name\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"body\":\"We're a new organization focused on contributing to beneficial AI outcomes through coordination and bridge-building between technical and governance communities.\\n\\nWe've identified what we think is a critical gap: technical AI safety research and AI governance/policy operate with significant information asymmetries, each making assumptions about what the other is doing. This undermines both fields.\\n\\nWe've developed a framework for integration that includes:\\n\\n1. **Shared definitions & language** - Creating common terminology so technical and policy communities can actually understand each other\\n\\n2. **Research-to-policy pipelines** - Mechanisms for technical findings to inform policy (and vice versa)\\n\\n3. **Institutional coordination** - Helping safety teams and policy teams within labs, and researchers and practitioners externally, actually work together\\n\\n4. **Common metrics** - Evaluating both technical work and policies on whether they enable beneficial outcomes\\n\\nOur hypothesis: the organizations that figure out how to span both technical and governance domains will have outsized influence on how frontier AI development unfolds.\\n\\nWe're publishing our full framework here: [link to full document]\\n\\nWe're interested in feedback, collaboration opportunities, and hearing about similar work. What integration points do you see as most critical?\\n\\n- Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold\\nhalcyon-threshold.pagewell.app\\nmorgan@halcyonthreshold.org\"}"
rows.quote: Posted on Alignment Commons (introduced Halcyon Threshold + shared research)
